runs.text: Why is the cleanup that closes the file written right after opening it?
Writing the cleanup next to what needs it avoids forgetting it: any exit from the subprogram runs it.
So that it is not forgotten even if the subprogram leaves early.

justification.text: It runs on leaving, by any path: a
or an error that is propagated.
It does not run where it is written: it is kept and runs on leaving.

runs.text: Because that way the program is faster.

justification.text: It does not change the speed; it changes that closing does not depend on reaching the end.
